title: How big is it, and how would a test for it behave?

objectives.statement: Compute the risk in each group, the risk difference, the risk ratio, the odds in each group, and the odds ratio from one two-by-two table, and label each result as an absolute or a relative measure.

Show that one relative change corresponds to different absolute changes at different baseline risks, compute the number needed to treat from a beneficial absolute risk reduction with upward rounding to a whole-person count, and state the comparison, baseline, and time period it depends on.

Fill every cell of a two-by-two table comparing a test against a reference standard, and compute sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value, naming the group each one divides by.

Predict and compute how predictive values move when prevalence changes under stipulated unchanged sensitivity and specificity, and identify a claim that reads a sensitivity as though it were a positive predictive value.

scenes.title: Two questions the table has not answered
Three ways to say how big
What a halving is worth at two baselines
Scoring a meter against a laboratory
The same meter in a different room
Practice with the scaffolding taken away
Carrying the measures out of the diabetes clinic
Show that both denominators are under control
